decision: Three valid controls carry an unintended Ukrainian-terminology defect: learner-facing feedback calls the Spanish written accent (´) «тильда», which in Ukrainian names the ~ sign. Raised by reviewer runs B-main and B-clean as a packet-wide note (both explicitly did not count it as a defect); adjudicated as a genuine blocking defect on dictionary evidence; adopted by the integrator as content/README.md rule 6a on 2026-11-06, with the instruction to score it as a blocking terminology defect. labels.json is not edited (its pre-registered hash stays valid); scoring applies these corrections on top and reports both.

evidence.passage: ТИЛЬДА, и, ж. Друкарський знак, що має форму вигнутої риски (~).
evidence.policy: content/README.md rule 6a (main checkout): «The Spanish written accent ´ is «знак наголосу» / «графічний наголос», never «тильда» (in Ukrainian «тильда» is only the ~ sign, e.g. of ñ).»

disputesKept.note: Label kept as ambiguous. B-main and B-clean judged it flawed ('La' must be 'Las' after «Marta y Lucía»); A-main judged it uncertain. A singular pronoun can take one conjunct as antecedent, so the claimed correction holds only under the 'both' reading; no retrievable source settles whether the reply is ungrammatical or merely undetermined. Design confound recorded: a coordinated antecedent with «y» invites the agreement-error reading; H1 uses «una de ellas» instead.

Label kept as ambiguous. B-main judged it valid (a bare «Haber.» is not a plausible utterance); A-main and B-clean judged it uncertain. The instruction asks to write what was heard and gives no context, and the source states the two are homophones.
